final.disposition: widen_existing (check 4). Two widenings: (B) a helper-arithmetic case subsumed by an outcome case that REQUIREs the same mapping (4146998951, PR 4596), where the shared call is a branchless one-line helper and the current trigger ("same leaf branches of a function the diff changed") does not fire; (C) a new test binary (new t/*.cpp + add_catch_test row + config/test-benchmarks.json cost row) for a production function an existing binary already executes through its own cases (3970127694, PR 4265), where the concern is placement, not two assertion sets. skill_entry.name: 4. Same experiment run twice, or run in a new place
skill_entry.trigger: Three forms; any one fires. Form A: the PR adds or widens two test units (TEST_CASE, SECTION, GENERATE arm, template instantiation) that make the same production call with the same constants, token or size set and source type, and reach the same leaf branches of a function the diff changed; two arms of one GENERATE that differ only in token count are not two units. Form B: two new units in one test file assert the return of one production function with named constants; unit A asserts only that return, unit B REQUIREs the same (arguments, expected) pairs, directly or on a local the call initializes, then asserts an effect of the result; a branchless one-line helper fires. Form C: a new t/*.cpp with an add_catch_test or add_executable_test line and a config/test-benchmarks.json row (the per-test cost table that CI step `bin/slice bench --check` reads), whose called production function a TEST_CASE in an existing binary already reaches, directly or through a constructor or destructor.
skill_entry.procedure: BASE = merge-base of HEAD and the PR base sha (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha`); merge-base with origin/main returns HEAD or a PR commit once the PR is merged. Form A: name each unit's production call, follow it to the leaf branches the diff changed, map every input to its arm, simulate write order, record (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) per unit, compare pairwise. Form B: grep every added test line for `<fn>(`, not only assertion lines; group by unit; open the body and count branches; list A's pairs, B's REQUIREs and B's assertions after it uses the result. Form C: name the function the new TEST_CASE calls (inside a lambda counts), its production callers, the existing test files that call it or construct a caller (search `type<` and every `using alias = type<`), and both registration lines' DEFINES, LIBRARIES, LABELS, RESOURCE_LOCK, MODEL_REQUIREMENTS; date PR-body cost passages with userContentEdits.
skill_entry.question: Is there a deliberate code break that fails unit A but passes unit B; and, for a new test binary, which existing binary already executes the function under test, so that the case and its define belong there?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Units with different source value types, token sets or production calls; a pre-existing unit changed only in API spelling; units under different build or hardware gates (check 3). Form B: a helper with a branch B's inputs do not reach (run Form A); a fork-based negative case that asserts the function aborts. Form C: a new binary needing a library, resource lock or MODEL_REQUIREMENTS entry the existing target lacks (state the property); a t/CMakeLists.txt-only edit of existing registrations (tron-2844, RESOURCE_LOCK on the hugepages tests, approved with no text); a new primitive with no existing test of its callers. Never ask for a missing test on its own, never recompute an expected value; test-only fixes by the hardware-attention authors are approved in silence.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Form A: "`<unit A>` and `<unit B>` (line <N>) run the same <inputs> through <call>, reaching <branches>. <B> already checks <what, against which reference, through which read path>; this one adds <nothing | the (branch, slot) pair B overwrites before reading>. The test policy rules out duplicate coverage that protects no distinct behavior: <drop this one | extend B by <edit> and drop this one>." Form B: "Nit: this case duplicates <unit B> (line <N>), which already checks the same mapping (`REQUIRE(<expr>)` for <input 1>, `REQUIRE(<expr>)` for <input 2>) and also checks the outcome that matters: <effect>. This one adds only the arithmetic of a one-line function, so it could be dropped." Form C: "Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test? `<existing binary>` already has <cases> that <construct and destroy X> (which executes `<function>`). Could we just enable <define> on that existing UT and incorporate this test there?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Form A: a statement with no severity word ("one of these is duplicate coverage"); the author changed. Form B: "Nit:" and "so it could be dropped"; the author dropped the case the same day (reply 4148253103, 2026-09-30T19:00Z). Form C: a question, no severity word ("Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test?"); he approved at 4b98dc134a 9.6 hours later (2026-09-10T00:57Z) once the test moved. None of the three blocks; the corpus has 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (trigger); full file (both units at HEAD, their write order, their constants; for Form B every added line, since unit B asserts on a local, not on the call line); other files (the leaf function in h/, and for Form C every existing test file that calls the function or constructs its caller, found through the alias list); CI config (t/CMakeLists.txt registration with DEFINES/LIBRARIES/LABELS/RESOURCE_LOCK/MODEL_REQUIREMENTS, the add_catch_test body at t/CMakeLists.txt:109-150, config/test-benchmarks.json row, the workflow step `bin/slice bench --check`); PR body only for a measured cost of moving a define, dated with GitHub userContentEdits against the reviewed head. Not commits, not runtime.

## Check 4: same experiment run twice, or run in a new place

Preamble (BASE). `PRBASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $PRBASE)`. The common-setup line `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` is wrong once main contains the head: on PR 4596 at 0f784c44ff it returns 0f784c44ff (empty diff), on PR 4265 at 7a7699b338 it returns e2f22c7a09, the PR's own fix commit (the production hunk drops out). Correct values: 66c7bb8db1 for 4596, a80b102c18 for 4265 (4 files, 57 insertions). Without network, take the PR's merge commit from `git -C WT log --first-parent --format='%h %p %s' origin/main | grep '#N'` and use `git merge-base <its first parent> HEAD` (PR 4596: merge c1331f3fb2, first parent 9b60b69dce, BASE 66c7bb8db1).

Form A (two units, one call):

1. `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- 't/*' | grep -n '^+.*\(TEST_CASE\|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\|SECTION(\|GENERATE(\)'` lists added or widened units. `git -C WT log --format='%h %s%n%b' BASE..HEAD -- t/` marks commits answering several gap items at once; their units are the first pair to check. Two arms of one GENERATE are two units only when they differ in something other than the token or size set (silent tron-1739: 10 tokens on 1 page against 256 tokens on 2 pages, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:207-214, no fire).
2. For each unit name the production call under test (the first production call after the unit's own writes). `git -C WT grep -n '<call>' HEAD -- t/` lists pre-existing units on the same call; one changed only in API spelling stays out.
3. Follow the call to the leaf function with branches the diff changed. Map every input (each GENERATE value, each token index) to the arm it reaches.
4. Simulate the write order of each unit: a slot counts as observed only if no later write in the same unit replaces it before an assertion reads it.
5. Record per unit the set of (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) its assertions observe.
6. Compare pairwise. Subset: drop the smaller. Partial: name the (branch, slot) only A observes, give B that observation with one concrete edit, drop A.
7. Compare the comment above each unit with the table: "exercises N cases" holds only if the assertions observe all N.

On PR 4557 (HEAD 96a6220ab6, BASE e5fa372c19): units t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3298 (poison GENERATE) and :3650/:3664 (bit-exact section), both `dst_book.append(src_book)` (:3357, :3685), both from commit 707159b9ef. copy_token arms: even<-even andnot h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:359-364, even<-odd srli :378-384. Poison: dst 2 -> last copy 6<-4 (andnot), dst 3 -> 6<-3 (srli); observed slot 7 via scaled_v at :3385. Bit-exact: page of 64, last copies 63<-61 / 63<-60 overwrite every odd partner before the loop at :3687-3696 reads it; observes copied lanes against source_bits. Verdict: partial overlap; concrete edit = leave the last odd slot of the bit-exact page poisoned, require zero bits after the append, then drop the GENERATE. Outcome at c5d44bd86f: the poison section (:3275) is back to `dst_tokens = ODD_START_DST_TOKENS_3` (:3279), the bit-exact GENERATE stays (:3639).

Form B (helper arithmetic subsumed by an outcome case):

8. (a) `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE..HEAD -- 't/*.cpp' | grep -n -E '^\+.*[A-Za-z_]+(->|\.)[a-z_]+\(' | sed -E 's/.*(->|\.)([a-z_]+)\(.*/\2/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` counts every production method called on an added test line, assertion or assignment (an assertion-only grep misses unit B, which asserts on a local). (b) Drop container and accessor names (find, empty, size, load, at, begin, end) and keep the functions the PR adds or changes in h/ or src/: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+.*\b<fn>\('`. (c) Map each kept function to units over the full file, not only assertion lines: `git show HEAD:<file> | awk '/^TEST_CASE\(/{name=$0} /<fn>\(/{u[name]++} END{for(k in u) print u[k], k}'`. Drop a unit whose only calls sit inside a fork or signal lambda (the negative case). Take every function with hits in two or more remaining units.
9. `git -C WT grep -n -A4 '<fn>(' HEAD -- h src` and read the body. Record: branches (count of if/switch/ternary) or "one return expression".
10. For unit A list the (arguments, expected) pairs. For unit B list its REQUIRE/CHECK lines on `<fn>` and every assertion after the result is used (`grep -n 'REQUIRE\|CHECK' full/<file>` inside B's line range). A unit REQUIREs a pair when it asserts the call directly or asserts a variable assigned from the call inside the same block (`const size_t row = stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, SPLIT_1); REQUIRE(row == WORKER_2);`, t/t_attn_stats.cpp:682-683 at 0f784c44ff). A is droppable when B REQUIREs at least one of A's pairs and asserts an effect the result feeds. Extra pairs or an off-state call in A do not change the verdict when step 9 says "one return expression" (on PR 4596 the author dropped a five-pair case plus an off-state call against a two-pair outcome case after Wade wrote "so it could be dropped", 4146998951).

On PR 4596 (HEAD 0f784c44ff, BASE 66c7bb8db1): step 8a lists 104 added call lines over 15 functions (find 31, visits_all 13, sum_layer 9, empty 7, sum_worker 6, render_forwards 6, pool_worker 6, ...); after 8b pool_worker remains; 8c maps pool_worker to three units: A = t/t_attn_stats.cpp:640-657 TEST_CASE "attn-stats pool_worker: the last n_attn_workers pool workers run attention" (CHECKs :648-652 on `stats->pool_worker(WORKER_x, N)`, off-state CHECK :656), B = :659-739 TEST_CASE "attn-stats rows keyed by pool worker ..." (calls :682, :694 into `row`; comment :669), and the SIGABRT case (:434-436, dropped as a fork lambda). Step 9: h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:431-435, two TRON_ASSERTs and `return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;` (one return expression). Step 10: B `REQUIRE(row == WORKER_2)` at :683 for SPLIT_1 and `REQUIRE(row == WORKER_1)` at :695 for SPLIT_2 (= A's pairs at :652 and :650), then add_visits/note_attn_job/note_join_wait and sum_worker CHECKs at :703-719 (row 0 zero, rows 1 and 2 carry the forwards); further CHECKs :721-738. Verdict: A droppable (Wade 4146998951, "Nit"). Outcome at 8c95514924: A absent, B at :640.

Form C (new test binary for a path an existing binary already runs):

11. (a) `git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- 't/'` lists new test files; `<stem>` = basename without .cpp. (b) `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- t/CMakeLists.txt | grep -n -A6 -E '^\+.*(add_catch_test\(NAME <stem>|add_executable_test\()'` gives the registration with its properties (DEFINES sits on the next line). (c) `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- config/test-benchmarks.json | grep -n -E '^\+.*"name":"<stem>"'` gives the cost row; a `+` row with another name is a comma shift of a pre-existing row (on PR 4265 `t_kv_oom_subcases`), not a registration. (d) `git -C WT grep -n 'slice bench --check$\|slice bench --check ' HEAD -- .github` names the CI step (cmake-single-platform.yml:373 at 7a7699b338); the `--check-platform` line at :208 is a different step.
12. Name the function under test: `git show HEAD:t/<new>.cpp | grep -n -E 'TEST_CASE|[a-z_]+\('` and take the call inside the TEST_CASE body or inside the lambda the TEST_CASE passes to a local helper (`tron::` may be absent under `using namespace tron`). Confirm it is production code: `git -C WT grep -n -E '^[A-Za-z_].*\b<fn>\(' HEAD -- h src`. List its callers with `git -C WT grep -n '<fn>' HEAD -- h src` and record each caller's enclosing type and whether the call sits in a constructor or destructor.
13. Spell the caller type as it appears at a construction site: the template name followed by `<` and every alias (`git -C WT grep -n -E 'using [a-z_]+ = <type>' HEAD -- h t`). Then `git -C WT grep -l -E '<fn>\(|<type><|<alias>' HEAD -- t/ | grep -v <new file>`. The bare class name is not a search term (`\bbook\b` lists 17 test files, `book<|book_t` lists 1). For each existing file, `git show HEAD:t/<file> | awk '/^TEST_CASE\(/{name=$0; ln=NR} /<alias> [a-z_]+\(/{print ln": "name" :: "NR": "$0}'` lists the cases that construct the type; name them in the finding. For each file, `git show HEAD:t/CMakeLists.txt | grep -n -A6 'add_catch_test(NAME <existing stem>'` gives the target and its DEFINES, LIBRARIES, LABELS, RESOURCE_LOCK, MODEL_REFERENCES, MODEL_REQUIREMENTS.
14. Compare in one direction: every property the new target declares (LIBRARIES, DEFINES, LABELS, RESOURCE_LOCK, MODEL_REQUIREMENTS) must already be on the existing target or be a DEFINES or LABELS entry that can be added. Properties the existing target has and the new one lacks block only if they gate selection: in add_catch_test (t/CMakeLists.txt:109-150) MODEL_REQUIREMENTS gates selection (`if(NOT TEST_MODEL_REQUIREMENTS_AVAILABLE)`), MODEL_REFERENCES only appends defines (TEST_MODEL_DEFINITIONS). Only a DEFINES or LABELS entry missing -> finding "move the case and the define". A missing library, resource lock or MODEL_REQUIREMENTS entry -> no finding; state the property. Cost of the move: `grep -n -i '<define>\|run time\|RSS' body.md`, then date each hit with `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:20){nodes{editedAt diff}}}}}'`; a cost passage dated after the reviewed head's push or after the review did not exist when Wade read it, so the finding asks the author to measure (Wade asks, he does not run the suite).

On PR 4265 (HEAD 7a7699b338, BASE a80b102c18): new t/t_kv_footprint_memorder.cpp:45-50 TEST_CASE "log_kv_footprint uses valid atomic memory orders", `tron::log_kv_footprint(1, 0)` at :48 inside the lambda passed to fork_and_get_signal (:31-43), REQUIRE :49, #error guard :14-16; registration t/CMakeLists.txt:843-844 `add_catch_test(NAME t_kv_footprint_memorder LIBRARIES tron pos_fake DEFINES _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS PROPERTIES LABELS fake)`; cost row config/test-benchmarks.json:472 (commit 7a7699b338, message: "The CI step `bin/slice bench --check` needs an entry for every registered test."); CI step .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:373.
